title: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST)
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for GIST. Full pathway: workup and molecular typing -> clinical state (localized / unresectable-metastatic / progressed / recurrence / surveillance). Localized branch routes resectability -> mutation-directed neoadjuvant with a response gate -> surgery -> recurrence-risk stratification -> mutation-directed adjuvant with a completion gate -> surveillance. Advanced branch is a genotype-selected first line followed by a response / line-of-therapy sub-tree (first line -> response -> dose-escalate vs switch -> second-line sunitinib -> third-line regorafenib -> fourth-line ripretinib -> beyond). Systemic leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id where a GIST-specific dose card exists (imatinib / sunitinib / regorafenib); avapritinib and ripretinib are shown as guidance because the library holds no GIST-dose card for them. Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references; original wording, no proprietary guideline text reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references for GIST (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison). Original wording. Systemic-therapy leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses. No proprietary guideline text reproduced. Invents no dose or regimen.

a.text: Recurrence risk is estimated from tumor size, mitotic rate (per 5 sq mm / 50 HPF) and primary site; non-gastric (small-bowel, rectal) sites and tumor rupture carry higher risk at equal size and mitotic count.

b.text: For resected high-risk KIT-mutant GIST, adjuvant imatinib for at least 3 years improves recurrence-free and overall survival versus shorter courses.

c.text: PDGFRA exon 18 D842V is intrinsically imatinib-resistant; avapritinib is the preferred agent and imatinib offers no benefit. No GIST-dose card exists in this library for avapritinib, so it is shown as guidance.

d.text: Mutation testing (KIT exons 9/11/13/17, PDGFRA exon 18 including D842V, and SDHB IHC where KIT/PDGFRA wild-type) should precede any systemic decision, since genotype predicts TKI sensitivity and starting dose.

e.text: Assess TKI response by CT: a fall in tumor density (Choi-type response) can indicate benefit even without RECIST shrinkage; confirm true progression and rule out non-adherence before changing lines.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and diagnosis
nodes.description: Confirm GIST histology, define extent, and obtain molecular status before any treatment decision.

bullets.label: History, exam, performance status; GI bleeding / mass / obstruction symptoms
Contrast CT of abdomen and pelvis; chest imaging for staging
Biopsy with immunohistochemistry
bullets.sub: CD117 (KIT) and/or DOG1 positive; report mitotic rate per 5 sq mm

bullets.label: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsy for gastric / esophagogastric lesions when feasible
Molecular testing before systemic therapy
bullets.sub: KIT (9, 11, 13, 17), PDGFRA (exon 18 incl. D842V); SDHB IHC if KIT/PDGFRA wild-type

bullets.label: Multidisciplinary review with a sarcoma / GIST-experienced team

nodes.name: Clinical presentation
nodes.title: Clinical presentation / disease state
nodes.description: Choose the current clinical state; this selects the pathway (localized surgery, advanced systemic, progression sequencing, recurrence, or surveillance).

options.label: Metastatic, already progressed on prior TKI

nodes.name: Resectability
nodes.title: Localized: resectability assessment
nodes.description: Decide whether complete (R0) resection is achievable now with acceptable, function-preserving morbidity.
bullets: Tumors < 2 cm without high-risk EUS features may be observed with periodic endoscopy
Consider neoadjuvant TKI when downsizing would allow organ preservation (GE junction, duodenum, low rectum)
Avoid tumor rupture at surgery - rupture upstages any GIST to high recurrence risk

options.label: Very small (< 2 cm) incidental gastric, no high-risk EUS features
Marginally resectable - would benefit from downsizing

nodes.name: Small tumor - observe
nodes.title: Very small incidental gastric GIST: endoscopic surveillance
nodes.description: Sub-2 cm gastric GIST without high-risk features may be followed rather than resected.
bullets: Periodic endoscopic ultrasound to track size and echofeatures
Resect on growth, symptoms, or new high-risk features (irregular margin, cystic spaces, heterogeneity)
Shared decision-making; resection is reasonable if reliable surveillance is impractical

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant mutation status
nodes.title: Marginally resectable: mutation-directed neoadjuvant plan
nodes.description: Genotype predicts whether neoadjuvant imatinib will shrink the tumor before surgery.

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant imatinib
nodes.title: Neoadjuvant imatinib to maximal response
nodes.description: Imatinib to best radiologic response, then reassess for function-preserving resection.
bullets: Imatinib until best radiologic response, typically 6-12 months, monitored by CT
Confirm KIT sensitivity on the molecular report before starting
Do not wait for progression - operate at maximal response (next step is the response gate)
Continue imatinib perioperatively; resume the adjuvant course after recovery

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant response
nodes.title: Response to neoadjuvant imatinib
nodes.description: Restage after neoadjuvant imatinib; response determines whether resection now proceeds.

nodes.name: Resect after neoadjuvant
nodes.title: Resection after neoadjuvant response
nodes.description: Function-preserving resection at maximal response, then recurrence-risk stratification for adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Complete (R0) resection at maximal response; avoid tumor rupture
Resume imatinib after recovery; total peri-operative plus adjuvant exposure is individualized
Then stratify residual recurrence risk to set adjuvant duration (next step)

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant progression
nodes.title: Progression on neoadjuvant imatinib: treat as advanced disease
nodes.description: Progression or persistent unresectability converts management to the advanced-disease pathway.
bullets: Re-confirm genotype and adherence; rule out pseudo-progression by density before switching
Manage as unresectable / metastatic GIST - move to the advanced systemic pathway
Reconsider surgery only if later downsizing restores an R0 option
nodes.linkLabel: Continue in the advanced-disease pathway (systemic sequencing)

nodes.name: Resistant genotype - surgery
nodes.title: Resistant genotype: proceed to surgery
nodes.description: Imatinib is unlikely to downsize a D842V / resistant tumor; plan resection directly, then stratify risk.
bullets: Proceed to R0 resection if achievable; neoadjuvant imatinib offers no benefit for D842V
For D842V requiring downsizing, consider avapritinib in a trial / expert setting (no dose card here - guidance only)
Re-stage after multidisciplinary review, then stratify recurrence risk (next step)

nodes.name: Recurrence-risk stratification
nodes.title: Resected localized GIST: recurrence-risk stratification
nodes.description: After complete resection, estimate recurrence risk from size, mitotic rate and site to decide on adjuvant therapy.

tables.title: Risk of recurrence by size, mitotic rate and site (approximate)

nodes.name: Low risk - observe
nodes.title: Very-low / low risk: surveillance, no adjuvant therapy
nodes.description: Complete resection with low recurrence risk; adjuvant TKI is not indicated.
bullets: No adjuvant imatinib
History, exam and abdominopelvic CT every 6 months for 5 years, then annually
Return to the recurrence pathway on any new lesion (next step is the surveillance schedule)

nodes.name: Intermediate-risk decision
nodes.title: Intermediate risk: adjuvant imatinib or observe
nodes.description: Adjuvant imatinib is discretionary at intermediate risk; weigh site, mutation, rupture and patient factors.
bullets: Non-gastric primary or tumor rupture pushes risk toward the high-risk group - favor adjuvant imatinib
Confirm KIT sensitivity first; PDGFRA D842V derives no benefit and should be observed
Gastric, intact, KIT exon 11 intermediate tumors are reasonable to observe

nodes.name: Adjuvant imatinib (intermediate)
nodes.title: Intermediate risk: adjuvant imatinib
nodes.description: Adjuvant imatinib chosen for higher-risk intermediate features; then a completion gate.
bullets: Adjuvant imatinib, standard starting dose; typical duration at least 3 years
Confirm KIT sensitivity before starting; monitor tolerance and adherence
Surveillance CT during and after therapy (next step is the completion gate)

nodes.name: Intermediate - observe
nodes.title: Intermediate risk: observation
nodes.description: Lower-risk intermediate features (or D842V) followed without adjuvant TKI.
bullets: No adjuvant imatinib for gastric, intact, lower-risk intermediate tumors or D842V
CT abdomen / pelvis every 3-6 months for the first years
Enter the recurrence pathway on any new lesion (next step is the surveillance schedule)

nodes.name: Adjuvant mutation status
nodes.title: High risk: mutation-directed adjuvant decision
nodes.description: Adjuvant benefit depends on genotype; select the mutation class.

nodes.name: Adjuvant imatinib (KIT ex11)
nodes.title: High risk, KIT exon 11: adjuvant imatinib >= 3 years
nodes.description: Standard adjuvant therapy for the most imatinib-sensitive genotype; then a completion gate.
bullets: Adjuvant imatinib for at least 3 years at standard starting dose
Monitor tolerance, adherence, and for surveillance CT during and after therapy
Longer duration is under study for the highest-risk cases (next step is the completion gate)

nodes.name: Adjuvant imatinib (KIT ex9)
nodes.title: High risk, KIT exon 9: adjuvant imatinib (higher dose)
nodes.description: Exon 9 tumors are imatinib-sensitive but often need a higher daily dose; adjuvant course still >= 3 years.
bullets: Adjuvant imatinib for at least 3 years; exon 9 disease may warrant a higher daily dose - the dose engine computes it
Monitor the added toxicity of higher dosing
Surveillance CT during and after therapy (next step is the completion gate)

nodes.name: D842V - no adjuvant
nodes.title: PDGFRA D842V: no adjuvant imatinib, surveillance
nodes.description: D842V is imatinib-resistant; adjuvant imatinib is not indicated.
bullets: No adjuvant imatinib - the genotype predicts resistance
Close surveillance CT; avapritinib is the active agent if disease recurs (enter the advanced pathway)
Refer to a GIST expert center where available
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence: enter the advanced-disease pathway

nodes.name: Wild-type / SDH-deficient
nodes.title: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type or SDH-deficient: surveillance / referral
nodes.description: Adjuvant imatinib is generally not beneficial for wild-type / SDH-deficient GIST.
bullets: Adjuvant imatinib is not routinely recommended - limited benefit in wild-type / SDH-deficient disease
Refer to an expert center; consider SDH-deficient / syndromic workup (Carney triad, Carney-Stratakis, NF1)
Surveillance CT / MRI on an individualized schedule
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence: enter the advanced-disease pathway

nodes.name: Adjuvant completion
nodes.title: During / after adjuvant imatinib: completion vs recurrence
nodes.description: Adjuvant imatinib delays but does not eliminate recurrence; track completion and watch for relapse (often on stopping).
bullets: Complete the planned course (>= 3 years); recurrences cluster after stopping
Restage periodically; any new lesion is treated as advanced disease

nodes.name: Adjuvant completed
nodes.title: Adjuvant imatinib completed: continue surveillance
nodes.description: Planned adjuvant course completed without relapse; move to long-term surveillance.
bullets: Continue CT surveillance - recurrence risk rises in the first years after stopping imatinib
Re-confirm genotype at any relapse to guide re-treatment
Proceed to the standard surveillance schedule (next step)

nodes.name: Recurrence on adjuvant
nodes.title: Recurrence during / after adjuvant imatinib
nodes.description: Relapse while on or after adjuvant imatinib is managed as advanced disease, informed by timing.
bullets: Relapse off imatinib: rechallenge with imatinib is often effective - re-enter the advanced pathway
Relapse on adjuvant imatinib: treat as imatinib-refractory and advance the line of therapy
Re-confirm genotype; consider resection of isolated recurrence
nodes.linkLabel: Continue in the advanced-disease pathway (systemic sequencing)

nodes.name: Metastatic mutation status
nodes.title: Unresectable / metastatic: first line by genotype
nodes.description: Genotype selects the first-line agent and starting dose for advanced GIST.

nodes.name: First-line imatinib (KIT ex11)
nodes.title: Advanced, KIT exon 11: first-line imatinib
nodes.description: Imatinib is standard first-line for advanced KIT-mutant GIST; continue until progression or intolerance.
bullets: Imatinib continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Assess response by CT; a fall in density can indicate response without shrinkage
Consider metastasectomy of residual / oligometastatic disease at best response in selected patients
On any change, use the response gate (next step)

nodes.name: First-line imatinib (KIT ex9)
nodes.title: Advanced, KIT exon 9: first-line imatinib (higher dose)
nodes.description: Exon 9 disease responds to imatinib, generally at a higher daily dose.
bullets: Imatinib first-line; exon 9 tumors often benefit from a higher daily dose - the dose engine computes it
Monitor the additional toxicity of higher dosing
Assess response by CT; then use the response gate (next step)

nodes.name: First-line avapritinib (D842V)
nodes.title: Advanced, PDGFRA D842V: avapritinib
nodes.description: D842V is imatinib-resistant; avapritinib is the preferred first-line agent.
bullets: Avapritinib for PDGFRA exon 18 D842V-mutant advanced GIST
No GIST-dose card in this library - shown as guidance; the physician arranges the regimen
Monitor for cognitive effects and intracranial bleeding per label
Do not use imatinib for D842V (next step is the response gate)

nodes.name: Avapritinib response
nodes.title: PDGFRA D842V: response on avapritinib
nodes.description: Track disease on avapritinib; progression on a D842V-active agent means limited standard options.

nodes.name: Continue avapritinib
nodes.title: D842V controlled: continue avapritinib
nodes.description: Maintain avapritinib while the disease responds.
bullets: Continue avapritinib; monitor for cognitive effects and bleeding
Consider metastasectomy of oligometastatic residual disease in selected patients
Restage on schedule; switch only on confirmed progression

nodes.name: D842V progression
nodes.title: D842V progression on avapritinib: trial / multikinase TKI
nodes.description: Few standard options remain after a D842V-active agent; prioritize trials.
bullets: Enroll in a clinical trial where available - the preferred option
A multikinase TKI (e.g. sunitinib, regorafenib, ripretinib) may be tried, though D842V benefit is limited
Continue best supportive care; consider local therapy for symptomatic sites

nodes.name: Wild-type subtype
nodes.title: Wild-type GIST: sub-classification
nodes.description: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type GIST is heterogeneous; sub-classification changes workup and referral.
bullets: SDH-deficient (SDHB IHC loss): younger patients, gastric, multifocal; Carney triad / Carney-Stratakis
NF1-associated or BRAF-mutant: distinct biology and drug sensitivity

nodes.name: SDH-deficient GIST
nodes.title: SDH-deficient GIST: expert referral, individualized therapy
nodes.description: SDH-deficient disease is typically TKI-refractory and indolent; manage at an expert center.
bullets: Refer to a sarcoma expert center; genetic counseling (SDHx germline, Carney triad / Carney-Stratakis)
Standard KIT-targeted TKIs are usually ineffective; sunitinib or regorafenib may give some benefit
Enroll in a clinical trial; surgery for symptomatic / oligometastatic disease
Often indolent - a watchful approach can be appropriate

nodes.name: Advanced wild-type (NF1/BRAF)
nodes.title: Advanced, NF1 / BRAF / other wild-type: trial / targeted
nodes.description: Non-SDH wild-type GIST is often TKI-refractory; pursue trials and any actionable target.
bullets: Refer to a GIST expert center; enroll in a clinical trial where possible
BRAF V600E: consider BRAF-directed therapy (guidance - no GIST-dose card here)
NF1-associated: KIT-targeted TKIs are typically ineffective; surgery for resectable disease
Multikinase TKIs (sunitinib, regorafenib) are options on progression

nodes.name: First-line response
nodes.title: Advanced KIT: response on first-line imatinib
nodes.description: Track disease on first-line imatinib; the pattern of progression (focal vs generalized) drives the next move.
bullets: Confirm true progression by CT (size and density); rule out non-adherence
Limited / focal progression is treated locally while continuing imatinib

nodes.name: Continue imatinib
nodes.title: Durable response: continue imatinib +/- metastasectomy
nodes.description: Maintain first-line imatinib while the disease responds; consider surgery of residual disease.
bullets: Continue imatinib indefinitely - stopping in responders leads to rapid regrowth
Consider metastasectomy of residual / oligometastatic disease at best response in selected patients
Restage on schedule; return to the response gate on any change

nodes.name: Focal progression
nodes.title: Limited progression: local therapy, continue imatinib
nodes.description: For focal progression with otherwise controlled disease, treat the progressing site and stay on imatinib.
bullets: Resection, ablation (RFA), or radiotherapy to the progressing lesion
Continue imatinib - most disease remains sensitive
Switch systemic lines only when progression becomes generalized

nodes.name: Second-line decision
nodes.title: Generalized progression on imatinib: escalate vs switch
nodes.description: At generalized imatinib progression, either escalate the imatinib dose (esp. exon 9 / limited progression) or switch to second-line sunitinib.

tables.title: Sequential systemic therapy for advanced KIT-mutant GIST

nodes.name: Imatinib dose escalation
nodes.title: Imatinib dose escalation (interim)
nodes.description: Higher-dose imatinib can recapture control, especially in exon 9 disease, before switching agents.
bullets: Escalate the imatinib daily dose - the dose engine computes it; monitor added toxicity
Most useful for exon 9 tumors and for limited progression
On further progression, switch to second-line sunitinib (next step)

nodes.name: Second-line sunitinib
nodes.title: Second-line sunitinib
nodes.description: Standard second-line therapy after imatinib failure or intolerance.
bullets: Sunitinib after imatinib progression or intolerance
Monitor blood pressure, thyroid function, and hand-foot syndrome
Assess response by CT; on progression use the second-line response gate (next step)

nodes.name: Second-line response
nodes.title: Response on second-line sunitinib
nodes.description: Continue sunitinib while controlled; advance to third-line regorafenib on progression.

nodes.name: Continue sunitinib
nodes.title: Controlled on sunitinib: continue
nodes.description: Maintain sunitinib while the disease responds.
bullets: Continue sunitinib; manage hypertension, hypothyroidism, and hand-foot syndrome
Consider local therapy for a single progressing site while continuing sunitinib
Restage on schedule; advance the line only on generalized progression

nodes.name: Third-line regorafenib
nodes.title: Third-line regorafenib
nodes.description: Standard third-line therapy after imatinib and sunitinib.
bullets: Regorafenib after progression on imatinib and sunitinib
Monitor blood pressure, hand-foot skin reaction, and liver function
Assess response by CT; on progression use the third-line response gate (next step)

nodes.name: Third-line response
nodes.title: Response on third-line regorafenib
nodes.description: Continue regorafenib while controlled; advance to fourth-line ripretinib on progression.

nodes.name: Continue regorafenib
nodes.title: Controlled on regorafenib: continue
nodes.description: Maintain regorafenib while the disease responds.
bullets: Continue regorafenib; manage hypertension, hand-foot skin reaction, and hepatotoxicity
Dose interruptions / reductions per tolerance keep patients on therapy
Restage on schedule; advance the line only on progression

nodes.name: Fourth-line ripretinib
nodes.title: Fourth-line ripretinib
nodes.description: Switch-control TKI after three prior lines (imatinib, sunitinib, regorafenib).
bullets: Ripretinib after imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib
No GIST-dose card in this library - shown as guidance; the physician arranges the regimen
Monitor for alopecia, hand-foot syndrome, and hypertension
Assess response by CT; on progression use the fourth-line gate (next step)

nodes.name: Fourth-line response
nodes.title: Response on fourth-line ripretinib
nodes.description: Continue ripretinib while controlled; beyond progression, options are trials and palliation.

nodes.name: Continue ripretinib
nodes.title: Controlled on ripretinib: continue
nodes.description: Maintain ripretinib while the disease responds.
bullets: Continue ripretinib; manage alopecia, hand-foot syndrome, and hypertension
Consider local therapy for a single progressing site while continuing therapy
Restage on schedule; move to trials / palliation only on generalized progression

nodes.name: Beyond fourth line
nodes.title: Beyond fourth line: trial, rechallenge, best supportive care
nodes.description: After four TKI lines, prioritize clinical trials; TKI rechallenge and supportive care are palliative options.
bullets: Enroll in a clinical trial where available - the preferred option
Rechallenge with a previously effective TKI can give transient palliative benefit
Continue best supportive care; local therapy for symptomatic sites
Re-confirm genotype (resistance mutations) to match any available targeted trial

nodes.name: Prior line reached
nodes.title: Already progressed: which prior TKI?
nodes.description: For patients presenting after prior TKI failure, enter the sequence at the appropriate next line.
bullets: Confirm true progression and adherence on the last TKI before advancing
Re-confirm genotype; consider trials at every line

nodes.name: Recurrence pattern
nodes.title: Recurrence after resection
nodes.description: Distinguish resectable local recurrence from disseminated disease.
bullets: Re-image (CT chest / abdomen / pelvis) and re-confirm mutation status if not already known
Most recurrences are treated as advanced disease with systemic TKI

nodes.name: Resect recurrence
nodes.title: Isolated recurrence: resection + systemic therapy
nodes.description: Resection of isolated recurrence, usually combined with a TKI, then surveillance.
bullets: Resect isolated recurrence when complete removal is feasible
Start / resume imatinib for KIT-sensitive disease - most recurrent GIST behaves as advanced disease
Enter surveillance after treatment (next step)

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: Follow-up cadence after resection or during / after systemic therapy.
bullets: After resection of higher-risk GIST: CT abdomen / pelvis every 3-6 months for 3-5 years, then annually to 10 years
Low-risk resected GIST: less frequent imaging, individualized
On systemic therapy: periodic CT with response assessment; watch for progression to change lines
Any new lesion returns to the recurrence / advanced pathway
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence is detected: go to the Recurrence pathway
